findings.proposed_text: A criterion is confirmed by its passing recorded command (ShipLoop reruns them on done), not by this summary. For each completion criterion of the accepted step plan: check the implement result's per-criterion receipt, then rerun or inspect its confirmation on the current candidate; stale, missing or skipped evidence is incomplete. Name any confirmable criterion that failed or was not confirmed and do not accept the item. Report revise when a criterion reported `inspected`/`unconfirmable` needed execution by its `Confirm by:`, or is proven unachievable (product-wide: replan at an OUTER stage). Compare the actual diff and affected consumers with the accepted plan (Coding decision guide), and check the static-checks entry-point inventory covers every entry point in the diff. Classify every selected case and affected requirement clause as passed, failed, blocked, not-run or justified N/A with its checked surface and evidence; a pass at another surface, or source/DOM structure for a rendered interaction, is supporting evidence, not closure; never claim all requirements met while due observations are unrun. If the item selected a service, verify its due outcomes and failure cases per Service discovery guidance, separating local simulation from remote readback. This is item acceptance, not integration or release.

cross_cutting: Heads are the packet: in this run the model opened 1 of 22 packet files and saw 265-1922 chars of each head (it truncated with head -c / sed). Every operation the stage's check depends on must be in the head: skill-assess and skill-validate have no Considerations line at all (stage_spec has no develop/test), static-checks' quality-loop Start command and receipt are body-only, and integration-verify's Considerations line just repeats the goal.

Code craft (3,688 chars) is attached to document, verify and integrate although their guidance never refers to it (document edits docs only; verify reviews; integrate commits). Remove 'code-craft' from those stages' blocks in shiploop_stage_spec.py (keep a 2-line docstring/comment excerpt for document). It stays where code is fixed: static-checks, integration-verify.

The Improve sentence in COMMON ('Only planning results ... get an actual Improve-skill handoff ... advances directly') plus the bottom 'Improve: This result advances directly; no Improve child runs' appear in every non-Improve stage: they state what does NOT happen (owner rule: mention Improve only as a directive). In carry-forward/system-test-author the bottom line is the directive and the COMMON sentence duplicates it.

The 1,920-char workspace return block (plan-return, review-return, return route, receipt) is printed in every inner stage while saying the return is unavailable there; at integrate it also conflicts with the stage's own commit rule ('commit the ones the product needs' vs 'commit nothing for the return except...'). Print a ~330-char boundary note outside release/handoff.

Check-type duplication: the 'ShipLoop reruns every recorded command' gate is stated in Checked by, in stage text (verify 260-262) and in the Test rerun block; Allowed outcomes are restated in static-checks' Report paragraph and PASS_OR_STOP step (3). Keep the head copy plus the command list; the body should give only how to satisfy it.

Lint blocks print raw audit material: 13 lines of git plumbing (1.2k) and stdout/stderr '(empty)' pairs at static-checks; at verify an unchanged 0-finding record is reprinted word for word and asks for dispositions of no findings. Print plumbing and empty output only on failure, and a one-line summary when nothing changed.

Within-packet shared-core duplicates in every packet: the complete command twice (top + 'Call this when done'), the Scratch//tmp rule twice, the awaiting/no_default schema twice (outcome shapes + COMMON unattended paragraph) plus a third blocked hint in the Improve line, run-inline/recovery three times, current stage named 5 times, and the step-plan result listed in 'Results this stage builds on' and again as a 6-line 'source' record.

Stage guidance text is generally written for the worst case (services, remote boundaries, skills, baselines) with conditions implicit; making the conditional ones explicit ('If the item selected a service...') lets them shrink without dropping obligations, and gives a fresh model a clear N/A path, which is what most of these stages produced in this run.
